answer: Continuity-signed interaction ledger. Each identity must raven its full message history as a hash chain, and peers refuse service unless every prior signature verifies against the chain’s genesis. An attacker cannot forge a convincing chain without replaying real elapsed interactions, because each entry is co-signed by the counterparty who anchor their own chain to it. Cloning costs the attacker a full history of distinct, mutually confirmed exchanges plus the compute to keep each chain synchronized.
